Overview: Migraine is primarily neurovascular, involving dysregulation of trigeminovascular pathways, cortical excitability, and neuromodulatory systems
Symptoms: Throbbing one-sided headache, nausea, sensitivity to light/sound, visual aura (zigzag flashes), worsens with activity, neck stiffness.
Causes: Migraine is a hereditary disease with both monogenic and polygenic forms. Migraine has a strong genetic basis and is influenced by both genetic predisposition and internal and external factors . Low neuronal hyperexcitability, often referred to as "the migrainous brain," is influenced by genetic predisposition. Certain internal and external stimuli can influence migraine frequency and severity, though the evidence for many is inconsistent
Preventions: Migraines are characterized by an increase in frequency, severity, and duration of migraine attacks.
Treatment: Over-the-counter analgesics, over-the-counter analgesics, antiemetics, and migraine medications.
When to See a Doctor: Consult with a healthcare professional if you are experiencing new onset of severe headaches or accompanied by fever, stiff neck, confusion, or neurological deficits (e.g., weakness, vision changes) . These could indicate more serious underlying conditions.
